children: Merck received a positive CHMP opinion recommending EU approval of Keytruda plus Padcev as perioperative therapy for resectable MIBC, including SC Keytruda. European Commission decision is pending, with a final outcome expected by Q4 2026.
Material Details
Detail
AI Analyst View
Positive CHMP opinion for MIBC combo
De-risks EU approval for a potential new perioperative standard, expanding Keytruda’s addressable market.
Applies regardless of cisplatin status
Broader eligible pool could lift uptake versus cisplatin-limited options.
EC decision expected by Q4 2026
Sets timeline for potential EU revenue inflection; regulatory overhang remains until EC acts.
Based on Phase 3 KEYNOTE-B15
Trial showed 47% EFS risk reduction and 35% OS benefit vs chemo, supporting clinical value.
Includes Keytruda SC formulation
Subcutaneous option can ease administration, aiding adoption and persistence.
U.S. approval already granted
Validates regimen commercially; EU nod would extend geography and sales.
Context by AI Analyst

This is a late-stage regulatory milestone extending Keytruda’s expansion into earlier bladder cancer settings, aligning with its perioperative strategy. A binding EC approval, label details, pricing/reimbursement, and rollout pace will determine the magnitude of the commercial impact.
Based on the original press release from Merck & Co., Inc., Rahway, N.J., USA distributed by BusinessWire.
